- microG can be installed instead of Google's apps. Pick it from the release
  list (or `-release microg` on the command line). One microG release covers
  Android 13 and newer, and it updates on its own as microG does
- The microG release includes microG Services, its Services Framework proxy and
  Companion, plus optional Aurora Store, Aurora Services and the F-Droid
  Privileged Extension, with presets for each combination
- microG installs to /system, sets itself as the network location provider, and
  cleans up after the old standalone microG installer. It needs a ROM with
  signature spoofing
